To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the collective calcium response of a cell culture is regulated by mechanical forces and that the frequency of calcium responses is independent of the stiffness of the substrate.

1) the ATP-induced calcium response of cells is affected by the mechanical properties of the substrate, 2) the collective behaviour of cells in a two-dimensional culture on a substrate is determined by cell–cell contacts, and 3) the frequency of calcium responses depends on ATP concentration.

(i) the collective calcium oscillatory response of fibroblasts depends on cell–cell contact and (ii) the mechanical properties of the substrate affect the frequency and amplitude of the collective calcium response.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the role of mechanical forces in the regulation of collective cell behaviour.

the role of mechanics in collective calcium signalling in cell cultures.
